messages:
maria_g: forwarding a ticket from a customer hitting 413s when uploading a large embeddings batch. they're using streaming and getting intermittent "413 Payload Too Large" after ~32s of upload. pasted logs below. can someone confirm typical request size/time limits and best-workaround patterns?

maria_g: customer report (redacted) ->
> upload job id: job_9XY
> endpoint: POST /v1/embeddings/stream
> payload: newline-delimited JSON, ~200k items, ~120MB total
> error: HTTP/1.1 413 Payload Too Large
> server-msg: "request body exceeded maximum allowed size"
> client: node fetch streaming, no explicit Content-Length (chunked)

alex_k: thanks, maria. first-pass: 413 usually means the gateway rejected the overall request body size. streaming chunked uploads still have backend limits aggregated by the ingress. we have a soft limit of ~10MB per request body (API gateway) before it rejects. we should confirm exact number with infra, but customer at 120MB is way over.

jonp: adding eng-runtime context — when customers use the streaming embeddings endpoint we support two common patterns: 1) multiplexed streaming (open-ended single HTTP stream, server emits partial responses) and 2) chunked-batch POSTs (client splits into many small POSTs). Our gateway does not allow single-upload > 10MB. streaming/transfer-encoding: chunked still accumulates. so recommend chunking client-side into batches <= 8MB (payload) or <= ~2k items depending on item size.

maria_g: customer specifically wants to avoid reassembling at their side — they wanted to stream NDJSON as a single stream. is there a recommended pattern we can give them that minimizes rework?

jonp: yes. two options to propose: 
1) Multipart/stream-of-batches: send many sequential POSTs to /v1/embeddings with Content-Type: application/json, each containing an array of, say, 500-2000 records (tune by avg text length) and collect responses server-side. This is friendly to gateways and retries per batch.
2) Use the upload-object API (presigned object) for very large datasets: upload to S3-compatible staging, then call a single manifest call that references the object. This avoids HTTP body limits entirely. We have a helper in the SDK for this (redeem-upload-token).

sre_jen: infra confirm: gateway hard limit is 10_485_760 bytes (10MiB) per request. chunked transfer still enforced — we buffer up to that size and then reject with 413. Also note stable connection timeouts at ~60s for streaming calls. so the pattern should be batching + backoff.

alex_k: also important: batching affects throughput and model memory. for embeddings, batching many small inputs is faster, but extremely large batches cause timeouts. recommend targeting 2-5k tokens total per batch or empirically target ~4-8MB payload. show them an example client snippet.

maria_g: customer also saw a "dimension mismatch" error on a later run: 
> 400 Bad Request - Dimension mismatch: model 'redwood-embedding-1536' expects 1536 dim vectors but received 768

alex_k: that one means they tried to dedupe/merge embeddings from two different models or used an older embedding model. tell them to confirm the model param in their pipeline (and the vector length returned by the SDK). we should ask for a sample response that generated 768-length vector.

maria_g: relaying recommended repro steps to customer (need them to run these and paste outputs):
1) run a small batch (5 items) to embedding endpoint with explicit model param and paste the full response. e.g.
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embedding-1536","input":["a","b","c","d","e"]}'
```
2) run a chunked POST test: split their dataset into files <=8MB and POST sequentially. report which batch index first returns 413.
3) if using streaming, capture the client-side code that opens the stream (show us headers) — especially Content-Type and whether they send Content-Length.
4) include the exact request-id/x-request-id from failing responses (we can trace).

jonp: i'll add a troubleshooting checklist for our docs based on this: recommended batch sizes, example python/node pseudocode, retry/backoff guidance, and manifest/upload alternative. short example (python generator streaming smaller POSTs):
```python
# pseudo: split generator -> POST each batch
def batchify(iterable, batch_size):
    batch = []
    for item in iterable:
        batch.append(item)
        if len(batch) >= batch_size:
            yield batch
            batch = []
    if batch: yield batch

for i, batch in enumerate(batchify(source, 1000)):
    r = requests.post(URL, headers=headers, json={"model":"redwood-embedding-1536","input":batch})
    if r.status_code == 413:
        print("413 at batch", i); break
    r.raise_for_status()
```

sre_jen: also monitor response headers on failures: we include X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining, plus X-Request-Id. for 413 we don't provide Retry-After because it's a client-size problem, not transient. for the customer we can recommend incremental binary search on batch size to find the maximum allowed batch (some inputs compress better).

alex_k: action items for us: 
- jonp: add doc snippet + sample SDK helper for chunking (small PR).
- eng-infra/sre_jen: confirm exact gateway limit in public docs (10MiB figure).
- support/maria_g: send the quick-check list to customer and ask for request-id and smallest repro that fails.

maria_g: i'm sending the checklist now. will update thread when customer responds. thanks all. :rocket:

ingest-bot: Note: queued follow-up ticket autoposted -> internal case 83421 linked to job_9XY

maria_g: UPDATE (customer reply): tried chunking into 4MB parts; first 4MB parts succeeded, then at batch ~320 they saw 413 on one batch. they included x-request-id: rq_4c7f and server debug snippet: 
> upstream: nginx-ingress-2 -> 413 at buffer: 10485760

jonp: that looks like the gateway buffering variant — the 10MiB threshold hit after some streaming headers. ask them to reduce further to 2-3MB per batch or switch to upload-object flow. also ask whether they gzipping payloads (we support gzip) — compressed size counts for limits? yes, it's the post-encoded bytes that matter.

maria_g: customer will try 2MB batches and report back.

sre_jen: i added a note to incident runbook to call out 413 behavior and suggested workaround for very-large embeddings jobs (upload->manifest). will follow up on public docs update.

maria_g: closing loop for now. if the customer still fails on 2MB we'll escalate to infra with rq_4c7f trace.
